prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel (alarms used with personnel reports); Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: switching after state check + Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace; readiness checked. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): telemetry→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment; incident log; single offshore contact. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis/authorization; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner; material changes→Rescue Coordinator. Metocean Buoy: site measurements. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. CTV: Harness Audit Card; suspended beyond limits. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Personnel: Marine Coordinator sets expected count, tracks vessels; Vessel Master verifies aboard; North/South Access Scanner; Personnel Tracking Console verified total; incident lead verifies headcounts. Discrepancy: Marine Coordinator pauses transfers, informs Shore Control Room, escalates to Duty Planner. Software: owner, approved baseline; SCADA Engineer verifies Firmware Hash Attestation; handover records change, limitations, contact. Emergency: Rescue Coordinator leads rescue/external aid; Field Supervisor directs site until transfer; Vessel Master vessel authority; HSE Officer advises; Operations Radio Console comms; Control Engineer remote shutdown; electrical recovery needs verified isolation; plans

New part:
S634: If conditions exceed the approved operating envelope, the Vessel Master may withdraw and the Rescue Coordinator revises the response plan.
S635: After an incident, personnel are accounted for, hazards are reassessed, and restart authority is assigned before normal work resumes.
S636: Vessel recovery support coordinates people, vessels, and handling equipment before any offshore recovery begins.
S637: The Rescue Coordinator establishes the recovery objective and confirms who has authority to suspend the operation.
S638: The Marine Coordinator assigns suitable vessels and maintains a common plan for their approach and departure.
S639: The Duty Planner confirms that the recovery task does not conflict with other offshore work.
S640: The Weather Service provides current forecasts for the recovery area and the planned transit route.
S641: The Weather Analyst interprets forecast uncertainty and identifies conditions that could affect safe vessel handling.
S642: The Vessel Master retains authority over vessel movements and may decline a task that cannot be completed safely.
S643: The Crew Transfer Vessel transports personnel and small equipment only when sea conditions and transfer arrangements are acceptable.
S644: The Daughter Craft may be assigned close-in support when its operating limits and communications coverage are adequate.
S645: The Service Operations Vessel provides a stable working platform when the response requires additional deck space or lifting capability.
S646: The Rescue Coordinator uses the load sheet to confirm that recovery baskets are secured and their contents are accounted for before transfer.
S647: The HSE Officer reviews the handling method, lifting points, and exclusion zones before loads are moved.
S648: The Personnel Tracking Console supports confirmation that all assigned personnel have returned to a safe location.
S649: The Field Supervisor maintains control of the work area and stops handling if personnel enter a restricted zone.
S650: The Electrical Technician isolates and protects recovered electrical equipment before it is placed in temporary storage.
S651: The Blade Specialist identifies fragile blade components and specifies padding or restraints to prevent handling damage.
S652: Recovered equipment is kept separated from loose debris and is secured against sliding, impact, and spray exposure.
S653: Damaged or contaminated items are contained so that they cannot create hazards for personnel or other cargo.
S654: Lifting gear is inspected before use, and each lift is conducted within the rated capacity of the equipment.
S655: The Warehouse System is used to arrange receiving space and preserve traceability for equipment returned ashore.
S656: The Spares Hub is consulted when recovered components may be needed to support repair planning.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
